objects.original: Actual normalized Gibbs initial phase law, actual finite prescribed density rho=q*terminal survival, actual Gamma endpoint, strict simplex comap volume, endpoint-pair pushforward L and flipped swap J.
objects.reconstructed:
E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed additive commutative group, with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume. V:E->R is the potential. alpha,beta are nonnegative real numbers and eta is real. States z=(x,v) lie in E x E; y and r are arbitrary points of E, with r the fixed reference point.
For a reference r, put g_r(x)=gradient V(x)-gradient V(r) and c_y,r=y-eta*gradient V(r). The deterministic state map is Phi_y,r(t,(x,v))=(c_y,r+cos(t)*(x-c_y,r)+sqrt(eta)*sin(t)*v, -sin(t)/sqrt(eta)*(x-c_y,r)+cos(t)*v), for every real t. All multiplications of vectors by real numbers are scalar multiplication.
S_r(x,v)=(x,v-[2*inner(v,g_r(x))/norm(g_r(x))^2]*g_r(x)). The rate is lambda_r(x,v)=sqrt(eta)*max(0,inner(v,g_r(x))). For u>=0, Lambda_y,r(z,u)=the real Lebesgue interval integral from 0 to u of lambda_r(Phi_y,r(s,z)) ds.
Rec is the disjoint union of live records (a,z), with a>=0 and z in E x E, and a single stopped record. Hist(n) is the space of arrays of n+1 such records indexed by 0,...,n.
Delta(n,T) consists of real vectors (t_1,...,t_n) such that 0<t_1<...<t_n<T. Prefix(n,T) is the subtype of vectors satisfying this condition, not a further distribution on times. The inequalities come from strict monotonicity after prepending 0 and the upper bound on every coordinate. Define tau_0=0 and tau_i=t_i for 1<=i<=n.
For a prefix and an initial state z_0, define z_i=S_r(Phi_y,r(tau_i-tau_(i-1),z_(i-1))) for 1<=i<=n. These are the zAt values. K(j) is the live record (toNNReal(tau_j),z_j), j=0,...,n. In a valid prefix every tau_j is nonnegative, so toNNReal leaves these values unchanged.
qReal is the product, over i=1,...,n, of lambda_r(Phi_y,r(tau_i-tau_(i-1),z_(i-1)))*exp(-Lambda_y,r(z_(i-1),toNNReal(tau_i-tau_(i-1)))). q=ENNReal.ofReal(qReal). The exponential belongs inside each factor of the product. qReal contains the n event factors and survival through their preceding intervals, with no terminal survival factor yet.
liveTime(live(a,z))=a and liveTime(stopped)=0. For any history h, d(n,T,h)=T-liveTime(h(n)) in nonnegative reals, hence truncated subtraction. weight_y,r(live(a,z),u)=ENNReal.ofReal(exp(-Lambda_y,r(z,u))); weight_y,r(stopped,u)=0. The live record time a is not used inside weight.
Path(T) is the full function space from {s in nonnegative reals:s<=T} to E x E. For arbitrary h, Psi_y,r,z0,n,T(h)(s) starts with accumulator z_0 and visits j=0,...,n in ascending order: a live record (a,z) with a<=s replaces the accumulator by Phi_y,r((s-a),z), with subtraction performed in nonnegative reals before coercion to reals; a later live time or a stopped record leaves the accumulator unchanged. Thus the last qualifying record by index determines the result, not necessarily the greatest time for an arbitrary history.
Gamma_y,r,z0,n,T(t)=Psi_y,r,z0,n,T(K(t)). At a valid prefix time s it is Phi_y,r(s-tau_j,z_j), where j is the largest index with tau_j<=s. It uses the post-S state z_j at a recorded event time. rho(t)=q(t)*weight_y,r(K(t)(n),d(n,T,K(t))); for a valid prefix its terminal factor is ENNReal.ofReal(exp(-Lambda_y,r(z_n,toNNReal(T-tau_n)))).
R(x,v)=(x,-v). V_y(x)=V(x)+norm(x-y)^2/(2*eta). pi_y is volume.tilted(-V_y): its density relative to volume is ENNReal.ofReal(exp(-V_y(x))/I_y), where I_y is the real integral of exp(-V_y) against volume. gamma is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian on E.
m(n,T) is the comap of volume on the real vector space Fin(n)->R along the subtype inclusion Prefix(n,T)->(Fin(n)->R); it is the induced volume measure on admissible time vectors.
For fixed y,r,n,T, the input space is (E x E) x Prefix(n,T). A(z_0,t)=Gamma_y,r,z0,n,T(t)(T). B(z_0,t)=(z_0,A(z_0,t)). sigma is (((pi_y product gamma) product m(n,T)).withDensity((z_0,t)->rho_y,r,z0,n,T(t))). L=map(B,sigma) is a measure on (E x E) x (E x E), in initial-state, terminal-state order. J(z_initial,z_terminal)=(R(z_terminal),R(z_initial)).

domains.original: Finite-dimensional real Borel inner-product E including rank zero; H=E×E; n:Nat,T:NNReal; X=H×Prefix n T; L on H×H. No path-space topology is substituted.
domains.reconstructed:
V:E->R; alpha,beta in R>=0; eta in R. y,r,x,v in E. There is no positive-dimension assumption on E.
Phi has real time argument, whereas Lambda has nonnegative time argument. T and live record times are nonnegative reals; n is a natural number including zero. Raw prefix coordinates are real, constrained by the subtype.
Hist(n) includes arbitrary live/stopped arrays without sorting or consistency requirements; K constructs a specific entirely live and consistent history. Path(T) has no continuity, differentiability, or sample-path regularity built into its type.
qReal and Lambda are real-valued; q, weight and rho take values in extended nonnegative reals. All displayed product, density and pushforward measures are on the indicated spaces with the displayed coordinate order.
domains.evidence: Finite real Borel inner-product spaces represent the source Euclidean phase coordinate-free, including rank0. Arbitrary total Hist and Path functions are bookkeeping domains; actual K/Gamma are selected for the sector. No path-space regularity assumption is hidden.

quantifiers.original: All ambient parameters under six original binders; forall y r n T (equivalently forall n T y r), actual endpoint-pair MeasurePreserving. No public density, normalizer, witness, positivity, finiteness, integrability or measurable-map provider.
quantifiers.reconstructed:
The claim is universally parameterized by every E and each of the displayed compatible norm, real inner-product, finite-dimensional, measurable-space and Borel-space instances.
For every V, alpha, beta, eta satisfying all listed hypotheses, the conclusion holds for every y and r in E, every natural number n, and every T>=0. There are no restrictions linking y and r.
The Hessian hypothesis is universal over both x and v in E. Initial states and time prefixes are variables integrated in sigma; the conclusion is an equality of measures, not a pointwise assertion about every initial state.
There are no existentially chosen constants, cutoffs, events, or reference points in the conclusion. Every let binding is definitionally fixed.
quantifiers.evidence: All six source assumptions and universal y,r,n,T are reconstructed. z and event tuple are integrated variables in sigma, not a claim that every fixed initial state has an invariant endpoint law. The introductory prose's initial phase names the actual density parameter; its final explicit measure conclusion fixes the quantifier scope.

conclusion.original: Exactly actual normalized fixed-count endpoint-pair reversal measure preservation. Normalized initial law does not assert normalized sector mass.
conclusion.reconstructed:
For each fixed y,r,n,T, J is measurable on the paired-state space and Measure.map J L = L.
Equivalently, the weighted initial/terminal pair measure for the displayed fixed-n prefix construction is invariant under exchanging initial and terminal states and negating both velocities.
For every measurable set C of paired states, this implies L(J^(-1)(C))=L(C). The asserted object is the endpoint-pair measure L for each separate n. The conclusion does not explicitly assert invariance of a full path-space measure, of a time-vector measure, or of a sum over n.
The formal conclusion does not state L has total mass one, nor a normalized transition kernel or an all-event-count stochastic process. Such interpretations or further consequences require additional reasoning and are not part of this reconstruction.
conclusion.evidence: MeasurePreserving J L L is the exact measurable flipped-swap invariant endpoint-pair measure underlying the source single-count change of variables. It does not assert probability/finite sector mass or full process invariance. hsector is the explicit internal normalized parameter-sector ingredient.

scopes.original: Fixed finite count and finite deterministic horizon only. No sum over counts, full process invariance, signed operator identity, all-time jump reversal, restart or cost.
scopes.reconstructed:
The definitions preceding the final universal quantifiers depend on fixed ambient E,V,eta as indicated; y,r are subsequently arbitrary arguments. Within each y,r,n,T instance, A,B,sigma,L,J are local definitions and the final assertion is MeasurePreserving J L L.
For n=0, the time vector is empty and the prepended time list has only 0; the strict-monotonicity and coordinate upper-bound conditions are vacuous for every T including T=0. The product qReal is 1, K contains only (0,z_0), Gamma(s)=Phi_y,r(s,z_0), and rho is the single survival factor ENNReal.ofReal(exp(-Lambda_y,r(z_0,T))).
For T=0 and n>0, Prefix(n,0) is empty because 0<t_1<0 is impossible; sigma and L are consequently zero measures. For T=0,n=0, Lambda over the zero interval is zero, the density is 1, and A(z_0,t)=z_0, so the pair measure is supported on equal initial and terminal states.
For n>0 all event times are strictly interior: an event at 0, an event at T, or coincident event times is excluded. For valid prefixes each interval length is positive, and the terminal interval T-tau_n is positive; the n=0,T=0 interval may be zero.
Real division by zero is zero. If g_r(x)=0, the denominator in S is zero, its scalar quotient is zero, S(x,v)=(x,v), and the rate at that state is zero. The reflection definition therefore has no nonzero-gradient premise. eta>0 ensures sqrt(eta)>0, so its reciprocals in Phi and the 2*eta denominator in V_y are nonzero in theorem instances.
toNNReal and ENNReal.ofReal take positive parts. For valid prefixes toNNReal does not alter event times or interval lengths, and qReal is nonnegative because the rates are nonnegative and real exponentials are positive. For arbitrary histories d truncates a too-large final live time to zero; a stopped final record yields liveTime=0 and terminal weight zero. Psi ignores stopped records rather than itself forcing a stopped path.
The tilted-measure formula is totalized, not an extra probability-normalization premise: if its real denominator I_y were zero the pointwise real quotient would be zero. This reconstruction does not independently prove finiteness, positivity or normalization of that integral from the stated hypotheses. Real integral notation is the total Lean integral operation.
Rank-zero E is permitted. In that case every vector, displacement and gradient difference is zero, every rate is zero, and all n>0 event-product densities vanish. No explicit rank-zero exclusion or replacement formula is in the statement.
The packet reports compiled=true. This decoder has not run Lean, inspected proof code, or verified the compilation flag. It has not seen source text or identity, prior audits or repair proposals, and does not certify source fidelity. The packet itself and its approved definition context are the only mathematical input. Simplifications above are elementary deductions from those definitions and assumptions; no unstated source theorem or proof route is inferred.
scopes.evidence: Fixed n and finite nonnegative T only, including n0/T0 and empty positive-count zero-horizon sectors. Zero rates/normals and rank0 require no exclusion. The source's later series, signed identity, invariant process and L2 statements remain red.

constant_dependencies.original: eta and actual V,y,r retained. Position Gaussian penalty 1/(2eta), momentum 1/2, rate sqrt(eta), exact phase normalizer with C=(sqrt(2pi))^dim. No artificial normalizing factorial or hidden constants.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed:
alpha and beta are uniform global Hessian bounds, with 0<alpha<=beta and beta*eta<=1. They constrain admissible V and eta but do not occur in any of the displayed measure, density, path or reversal formulas.
eta occurs in the center c_y,r, sqrt(eta) factors of Phi and the rate, and the quadratic tilt V_y. V occurs in its gradients, gradient differences, Hessian hypothesis and tilt.
y affects the center, deterministic flow, integrated rate along that flow, trajectory-derived densities, endpoint map and pi_y. r affects the reference gradient, center, reflection and rate and thus their downstream objects. pi_y itself does not depend on r.
n controls prefix dimension, number of event factors, number of reflection updates and history length. T bounds the prefix, sets the path domain and endpoint, and supplies terminal survival. Neither n nor T has an upper bound.
The constants 0,1,2 and exponent 2 are literal and fixed: 2 in the reflection coefficient and in 2*eta in V_y; squared norms in the Hessian, reflection denominator and quadratic tilt; unit upper bound in beta*eta<=1. cos and sin use their literal real-time arguments with no additional frequency parameter.
The Gaussian and volume depend on the ambient Euclidean structure. The normalizing denominator I_y depends on E,V,y,eta. No dimension-dependent bound, unspecified multiplicative constant, asymptotic notation, or accuracy parameter occurs in the asserted measure-preservation identity.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Actual sqrt(eta) dynamics/rates, 2eta proximal penalty, unit Gaussian momentum and no factorial normalization are retained. Normalizer is the actual103 partition inverse; its equality is consumed without new constants, cancellation or extra finite-test assumptions.
